items.title: Loading progress is a nearly invisible hairline
items.what: The ShoeMoney loading screen shows 'Downloading the game' above a 1px gold rule that is the only progress indicator, lost on the black field under the glowing logo.
items.why: First 5–10 seconds on a phone (WebGPU/Three.js compile + assets) look frozen; players force-quit before the bout even appears.
items.how: Replace the rule with a 6–8px rounded, glowing gold fill bar centered under the logo, plus a short status ('Compiling…' / percent) so progress is obvious at a glance.

items.title: FIGHT button and auto-countdown contradict each other
items.what: Qualifier intro (and the rematch screen) place a large gold FIGHT/REMATCH button directly above 'STARTING IN 2/4/8'. Sticks are already visible and live.
items.why: New players freeze: tap or wait? Missed or accidental starts kill the opening tension of a point-karate bout.
items.how: Auto-start screens should drop the button and use a shrinking ring or giant numerals; rematch should be tap-only with the timer paused until the player acts.

items.title: Twin-sticks plus legend steal the portrait dojo
items.what: Every portrait fight frame has two oversized analog sticks and a full-width STANCE/TECHNIQUE legend bar occupying the bottom ~300px; fighters' feet sit on the bar and the 3D dojo is letterboxed into a short strip.
items.why: The cinematic night dojo and photoreal sprites—the game's visual hook—are minimized; jump/crouch reads become tiny and thumbs cover even more of the playfield.
items.how: Default to smaller sticks (Large controls already exists as a toggle), auto-hide the legend after first input, draw sticks at ~70% opacity, and reclaim 80–100px of vertical space for the Three.js scene.

items.title: Move list truncates with no scroll affordance
items.what: The TECHNIQUES overlay lists Forward/Back/Up then clips 'Roundhouse Kick' at the bottom with a fade and no scrollbar, chevron, or hint that Down techniques exist.
items.why: The HUD itself advertises ▼ down, yet players never see those moves, so they spam the 5–6 visible punches and the kit feels shallow.
items.how: Make the panel a scroll view with a thin gold scrollbar or bottom gradient + chevron; or tab the four directions so every move fits on 844px without scrolling.

items.title: IPPON lockup covers the scoring contact
items.what: The IPPON / name / technique name block is centered over the fighters, burying the spinning-back-kick contact and the white-gi reaction that the bloom/split-tone chain was meant to sell.
items.why: Point karate lives or dies on seeing the clean hit; a UI popup instead of a visible payoff makes scoring feel cheap.
items.how: Pin the IPPON treatment to the top third (with the score bar), freeze or slow-mo the 3D contact fully visible, and put a small technique label near the impact, not over it.
